heading: INT. ABANDONED CIRCUS - RINGMASTER'S WAGON - AFTERNOON

units.text: INT. ABANDONED CIRCUS - RINGMASTER'S WAGON - AFTERNOON
A painted wagon, faded to the color of old peaches, its walls hung with moth-eaten posters of lions and strongmen.
A cracked mirror.
A brass bed with a mangy leopard-print throw.
Afternoon sun slants through shuttered windows, and dust turns in the beams.
ARNOLD "THE MAGNIFICENT" PELLEGRINO, seventy, in a satin dressing gown and an immense waxed mustache, sits before the mirror applying greasepaint to a face that has long ago stopped taking it.
He hums, off key.
The door creaks.
He does not turn.
If you're the bailiff, I'm indisposed. If you're the ghost, you're late.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: The door opens fully.
A young woman steps in with a briefcase and a paper bag of sandwiches, blinking in the dimness.
This is CORINNE WACHOWIAK-BELL, twenty-eight, a real estate appraiser, in a gray pencil skirt and sensible shoes, and she is clearly the most out of place person who has ever entered this wagon.
Mr. Pellegrino?
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Arnold the Magnificent.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: I'm Corinne Wachowiak-Bell. I'm here about the lot.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: I know why you're here, my dear.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: I brought sandwiches.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: I never eat before a show.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: There's no show.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: There is always a show.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: She sets the sandwiches on the bed.
The leopard throw shifts and a cat's head pops out.
She jumps.
You have a cat.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: I have a leopard.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: That's a cat.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: She is thirteen years old and has eaten two assistants. Be kind.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: Corinne laughs, then stops, then laughs again, nervously.
She takes a step toward the mirror.
In it, her reflection stands beside his.
Mr. Pellegrino, the county wants to demolish the grounds. They sent me to appraise the equipment.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: The equipment.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: The wagons, the tent, the cannon.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: The cannon is not equipment. The cannon is a colleague.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: I'll need to measure it.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Measure her gently.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: I will.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: You have kind hands. I can tell.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: You can't tell that from the mirror.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Forty years in the business, child. Nobody lies to the mirror.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: He swivels on his stool at last and looks at her.
His eyes are very blue under the greasepaint.
Sit.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: I don't have a lot of time.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Nobody does. Sit.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: She sits on the edge of the brass bed.
The leopard stares at her.
She stares back.
When I was twenty-two, I swallowed fire in this very ring. Two thousand people on the benches. I breathed in, and for one second I forgot to be afraid. You know what that felt like?
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: Like winning?
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Like nothing. Like the moment before the heartbeat. That is what a circus is, Miss Wachowiak-Bell. A very expensive way to hold your breath.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: And now?
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Now the breath has run out.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: Corinne looks at her briefcase.
She looks at the posters.
She pulls out a clipboard and sets it on her knee.
Mr. Pellegrino, I'm going to be honest with you. This is not the kind of job I like.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: No?
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: No. I like houses. Kitchens, with granite. I like when somebody's moving in.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: Then why did you take this one?
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: They didn't give me a choice.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: That is the circus. They never do.
units.name: ARNOLD

units.text: A beat.
She smiles.
He winks.
The leopard rolls onto its back.
Outside, an engine coughs awake and a chain rattles against iron.
Corinne stands.
Arnold does not.
That'll be the cannon.
units.name: CORINNE

units.text: So it begins.
units.name: ARNOLD
